item.title: Jays have goal of more offense this season | Jefferson City News-Tribune
item.description:
The Jefferson City Jays had to grind out last season with their defense.
Now the Jays want to open it up a little bit more.
Jefferson City will look to blend the stingy defense with a more balanced offense when the season begins at 6:30 p.m. today at home against School of the Osage.

item.title: Capital City boys have new coach, players heading into opener | Jefferson City News-Tribune
item.description:
The Capital City Cavaliers enters the season with a boys basketball team that is overall inexperienced at the varsity level heading into Blair Scanlon’s first season at the helm of the program.
The Cavaliers graduated eight seniors, saw the departure of coach Ryan Fick — now the athletic director at Blair Oaks — and went to the team’s first district title game a season ago.

item.title: Shorthanded Blair Oaks to open season against Mexico | Jefferson City News-Tribune
item.description:
WARDSVILLE — For the first time in more than two decades, the Blair Oaks boys basketball team will start its season before Thanksgiving.
But the Falcons will not have 60 percent of their roster available to play tonight’s season opener.
With the Falcons’ football season still ongoing, only 11 players will dress for the varsity-only matchup against the Mexico Bulldogs. Tip-off is at 7:15 p.m. at Blair Oaks High School.

item.title: Blair Oaks girls have two wrestlers this season | Jefferson City News-Tribune
item.description:
The Blair Oaks Lady Falcons won’t win any girls wrestling duals this season.
But winning an individual state championship is very possible.
Blair Oaks will open its season by bringing its two wrestlers to the Versailles Invitational, which starts at 2 p.m. today.

item.title: Republicans mulls deal to fund the military, but limit operations in Iran
item.description: Top Senate Democrats and Republicans are considering a deal to fund the military, but cut off funding for future operations in the Iran war.

item.title: Missouri officials say 'minimal impacts' expected from Iowa hazardous materials detonation
item.description: Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe said minimal impacts are expected to Missouri if the Army detonates lead azide in Iowa.

item.title: Tanner Bridge Road in Cole County reopens after bridge replacement
item.description: Tanner Bridge Road in Cole County had been closed since February for a $2.1 million project to replace the bridge.

item.title: Austin Simmons named SEC Co-Offensive Player of the Week
item.description: Austin Simmons has been named SEC Co-Offensive Player of the Week following an impressive performance vs. Kentucky.

item.title: Caffey’s 22 not enough as Mizzou women’s basketball falls to Kansas State
item.description: Mizzou women's basketball lost its first game of the season by sputtering to 64 points against Kansas State on Sunday.
